 2                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Senator 

 3   Marchione to explain her vote.

 4                SENATOR MARCHIONE:   Thank you, 

 5   Mr. President.  

 6                I am really proud to sponsor this 

 7   legislation before us today that would establish 

 8   March 13th as "K9 Veterans Day" here in New York 

 9   State.  

10                In making this formal designation, 

11   our state can officially recognize all K9 heroes 

12   who courageously protect and serve New Yorkers.  

13   K9 Veterans Day is intended to honor the service 

14   and sacrifice of dogs that aid members of 

15   America's armed forces, law enforcement, and 

16   public safety.  

17                But why March 13th?  Well, 

18   March 13th is recognized as a milestone day in 

19   American service dog history.  It's reported that 

20   on March 13, 1942, the United States Army created 

21   its K9 corps.  

22                March 13th is also the day that Ape, 

23   a beloved 2-year-old Czech German shepherd -- he 

24   was a tactical service dog that had only been 

25   working for the FBI for two weeks -- was 


                                                                1383

 1   tragically shot and killed in the line of duty 

 2   during a law enforcement raid in upstate 

 3   New York.  

 4                Currently, at least 11 other states, 

 5   including Florida and New Jersey, officially 

 6   recognize March 13th as K9 Veterans Day, and it 

 7   is time that the Empire State join them.

 8                I give attribution to the late 

 9   Joseph White, a retired military dog handler who 

10   pioneered the nationwide effort to recognize 

11   March 13th as K9 Veterans Day.

12                You know, today police dogs, 

13   bomb-sniffing dogs, and search-and-rescue dogs 

14   are hard at work protecting and serving all 

15   New Yorkers.  They're loyal, brave, hardworking 

16   and dependable.  These words can only begin to 

17   describe our courageous K9 heroes.  

18                So I ask my colleagues today to 

19   support this measure, just as you did last year.  

20   And it's my hope that this bipartisan bill, which 

21   is sponsored in the Assembly by Assemblyman 

22   Angelo Santabarbara, will become law this year so 

23   we can honor our K9 heroes.  

24                Thank you.

25                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Thank 


                                                                1384

 1   you, Senator Marchione.  You will be recorded in 

 2   the affirmative.

 3                Senator Croci to explain his vote.

 4                SENATOR CROCI:   Thank you, 

 5   Mr. President.  

 6                Whether it's in New York State in 

 7   our subway stations, our train stations, our 

 8   airports, or it's overseas ensuring that IEDs 

 9   don't harm our troops on bases -- and regardless 

10   of the breed, whether it's a German shepherd or a 

11   Belgian Malinois or if it's a Labrador retriever 

12   or the mutt, which is -- in the traditional 

13   American sense, the mutts sometimes seem to be 

14   smarter and better, which is an American 

15   tradition, I think.  But these dogs become part 

16   of your family, they become part of your unit, 

17   they become part of your life, your daily life.  

18                And I think what we've seen in 

19   Brussels highlights how important it is that we 

20   have protective measures and that we continue to 

21   honor service dogs.  

22                But I would say that we have a 

23   higher duty in this state.  What happened in 

24   Brussels, what happened in Paris, what happened 

25   in San Bernardino will happen in New York again.  


                                                                1385

 1   And the question is, as a Legislature -- and the 

 2   question to our Governor, and the question to the 

 3   Assembly -- is what to we want to do before the 

 4   next attack.

 5                Mr. President, the working dog is on 

 6   the last line of defense, because the bomb is has 

 7   already been planted, the event has already 

 8   happened.  I think that we should, as a 

 9   Legislature, continue to be supportive and not 

10   only honor our working dogs, but maybe have the 

11   intelligence, have the resources, put the 

12   resources into ensuring that we're not 

13   ill-prepared for the next attack, and that we as 

14   a Legislature, every one of us, can go back our 

15   districts and look our residents in the face and 

16   say we have done everything we possibly can.

17                Thank you, Mr. President.  I'll be 

18   voting aye.
